subject: Capacity commit cadence & utilization-driven addendum
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex.park@tiltanalytics.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@tiltanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal window approaching — usage spike and commit options

Hey Rohan,

Quick note as we head into our Feb renewal window: Q4 usage spiked above our committed sustained rate (esp. nightly batch runs + weekend traffic) and we're seeing higher latency tail for some endpoints. Procurement asked me to surface options: do we increase committed GPUs, add burst pool capacity, or try a utilization-based addendum?

Can you share a recommended path tied to our recent utilization (I can attach last quarter totals) and a rough timeline for adding capacity so we can plan the PO?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Park
Head of ML Infrastructure — Tilt Analytics
alex.park@tiltanalytics.com
Attachments: tilt_usage_q4.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@tiltanalytics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window approaching — usage spike and commit options

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for sending the usage file. High level recommendation attached: run a blended approach for this renewal — a committed tranche sized to cover your 50th–90th percentile sustained throughput, plus a small reserved burst pool (pay-as-you-go-style) for nightly surges. That minimizes unit cost while preserving headroom for spikes.

Quick bullets: 
- Proposed committed add: +40 GPUs (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) to cover baseline growth and expected Q1 load.
- Reserve burst pool: 8–12 GPUs for scheduled nightly batches (auto-scaled, billed by-minute).
- Canary rollout: enable 10% traffic on the new tranche for first 72 hours, ramp to 100% over 7 days if latency and error rates are healthy.
- Pricing: we'll offer a stepped discount for multi-quarter commit; I included a sample PO cadence in the PDF.

I attached: redwood_recommendation_v2.pdf (proposal + cost math) and the tilt_usage_q4.csv you sent (annotated). Stephanie, Marcus — can you confirm the utilization buckets and any infra caveats?

Next steps: if Tilt agrees to the +40/+12 split we can lock a delivery week and send a commitment amendment for signature.

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood_recommendation_v2.pdf (PDF, 220KB); tilt_usage_q4.csv (annotated)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Alex Park <alex.park@tiltanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window approaching — usage spike and commit options

Adding the utilization math — attached spreadsheet has per-workload percentiles and effective GPU-hours per day. TL;DR: Tilt's 75th percentile sustained token throughput maps to ~32 GPUs for steady-state. The 95th percentile bump (mostly nightly) is equivalent to ~12 GPUs for ~3 hrs/day.

Inline summary:
- 50th percentile steady: 22 GPUs equivalent
- 75th percentile steady: 32 GPUs equivalent
- 95th percentile nightly peak: +12 GPUs for 3 hours
- Observed growth rate (3mo): ~8% month-over-month

Recommendation aligns with Rohan: commit +40 (covers growth and gives buffer), plus a 12-GPU burst pool to be auto-allocated for scheduled jobs. We should also enable prefix KV caching for their largest models — that will reduce token cost and reduce observed tail latency without additional GPUs.

I've attached compute_profile_v2.xlsx with the percentile breakdown and the proposed tranche timeline. Marcus — any constraints on making 12 GPUs available as a burst pool on the requested cadence?

—Stephanie
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: compute_profile_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 480KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Alex Park <alex.park@tiltanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Feb 2027 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window approaching — usage spike and commit options

Thanks — operational notes from infra:
1) We can provision the +40 tranche within two standard maintenance windows (target: week-of Mar 7) if the PO is committed by Feb 18.
2) Burst pool (12 GPUs) can be delivered same-day as tranche go-live if we allocate from our burst reservoir; otherwise lead time is ~5 business days.
3) Canary and autoscale: suggest the 72-hour 10% canary Rohan called out; also recommend a short canary for their scheduled nightly jobs (run the nightly batch on the new burst pool for 2 cycles before redirecting traffic).
4) Ops caveat: nightly batch concurrency can be optimized with job backpressure + per-tenant KV cache TTL tuning to reduce peak GPU-hours — Stephanie's caching suggestion will materially reduce required burst capacity (est. -15% peak).

I'll draft an internal playbook for this customer and attach it. If Tilt wants a hardened SLA on burst availability we'll need a 30% overcommit in our reservoir or a guaranteed tranche reservation (we can include a line item in the amendment).

—Marcus
Director, Inference Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: fleet_canary_playbook.md (MD, 6KB)

From: Alex Park <alex.park@tiltanalytics.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window approaching — usage spike and commit options

Team — thanks for the clear recommendations and the math, appreciated. Tilt is prepared to move forward with the +40 GPU committed tranche and a 12-GPU burst pool with the canary plan you outlined. Procurement will raise a PO; timeline target: tranche live W/C Mar 7.

A couple of asks before we sign:
- Can you include a one-quarter utilization addendum in the amendment that allows us to convert unused burst minutes into credit (we expect some variance during onboarding)?
- Please confirm final pricing matrix/discount tiers and the expected invoice cadence.

Once we get the amendment with the utilization clause and the PO template, procurement will route for signature.

Best,
Alex
Alex Park
Head of ML Infrastructure — Tilt Analytics
Attachments: none
